questions.q: What exercise does Cuddy recommend for handling stress with more courage?
a: Writing an essay about your top core value
Repeating positive affirmations every morning
Visualizing yourself succeeding on stage
Listing the worst outcomes you can imagine
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to choose one core value and write about why it matters to you.

questions.q: What did the study find about people who wrote about core values?
a: Their stress hormones did not rise under pressure
They recovered from stress more slowly than others
They reported feeling more anxious afterward
They performed worse on difficult tasks
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the control group's stress hormones rose in a stressful situation while the values group's did not.

questions.q: Which system pushes you to try new things and take opportunities?
a: The approach system
The inhibition system
The defensive system
The avoidance system
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the approach system drives adventure and is strong in outgoing people.

questions.q: How can you break out of a feeling of powerlessness?
a: Recall a past moment when you felt empowered
Avoid situations you cannot control
Focus on the tasks you still have to do
Ask others to reassure you about your abilities
questions.why: Lesson 2 says remembering a win activates the approach system and helps you feel in control again.

questions.q: What did Cuddy observe about students with poor posture?
a: They had the worst grades in her class
They spoke less often but more clearly
They preferred sitting at the front
They were more likely to ask questions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the students with the worst grades were the ones slumped, heads down, sitting at the edges.
